articles.title: Resilience and sustainability through the F-E-W-H Nexus - Part 1
articles.titleEn: Resilience and sustainability through the F-E-W-H Nexus - Part 1
articles.summary: The conflagration in the Middle East has revealed with uncompromising clarity the precariousness of global architectures and the perilous interdependence of nations. What commenced as a localized eruption has metastasized into a geopolitical cataclysm with planetary reverberations, destabilizing energy markets, dislocating alimentary supply chains, and imperiling the welfare of millions of migrant laborers who constitute the sinews of transnational economies. For the Philippines, geographically distant yet existentially entwined with the Middle East through economic lifelines, remittance streams, and diasporic connections, the crisis is not an abstraction but a palpable reality. It manifests in vertiginous fuel prices, inflationary convulsions in food and commodities, and the precarious plight of more than 2 million overseas Filipino workers whose livelihoods, dignity and security now hang precariously in the balance.

articles.title: Retailwinds delayed, so, nothing to fret
articles.titleEn: Retailwinds delayed, so, nothing to fret
articles.summary: Retail inflation has risen above the RBI's target, driven by fuel and food prices. Core inflation remains subdued, offering a better measure of underlying price pressures. The central bank is unlikely to hike interest rates soon, anticipating price stabilization. Energy prices are expected to trend lower, and commodity markets may return to oversupply. India's vulnerability to imported inflation is diminishing as global conditions improve.
